{{short description|Hamiltonian used in quantum physics}}

The '''Anderson impurity model''', named after [[Philip Warren Anderson]], is a [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]] that is used to describe [[magnetic impurity|magnetic impurities]] embedded in [[metal]]s.<ref name=Anderson1961>{{cite journal |first=P. W. |last=Anderson |author-link=P. W. Anderson |title=Localized Magnetic States in Metals |journal=Phys. Rev. |volume=124 |issue=1 |year=1961 |pages=41–53 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.124.41 |bibcode = 1961PhRv..124...41A }}</ref> 
It is often applied to the description of [[Kondo effect]]-type problems,<ref name="Schrieffer-Wolff">{{cite journal|last=Schrieffer, J.R.|author2=Wolff, P.A. |title=Relation between the Anderson and Kondo Hamiltonians|journal=Physical Review|date=September 1966|volume=149|issue=2|pages=491–492|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.149.491|bibcode = 1966PhRv..149..491S |s2cid=55838235 }}</ref> such as [[heavy fermion]] systems<ref name="Hewson1993">{{cite book |first=A. C. |last=Hewson |title=The Kondo Problem to Heavy Fermions |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=New York |year=1993 }}</ref> and [[Kondo insulator]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dzero |first1=Maxim |last2=Xia |first2=Jing |last3=Galitski |first3=Victor |last4=Coleman |first4=Piers |date=2016 |title=Topological Kondo Insulators |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031214-014749 |journal=Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics |volume=7 |pages=249–280 |doi=10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031214-014749 |arxiv=1506.05635 |s2cid=15794370 |issn=1947-5454}}</ref> In its simplest form, the model contains a term describing the kinetic energy of the conduction electrons, a two-level term with an on-site Coulomb repulsion that models the impurity energy levels, and a hybridization term that couples conduction and impurity orbitals. For a single impurity, the Hamiltonian takes the form<ref name="Anderson1961" /><ref name="Schrieffer-Wolff" />

:<math>H = \sum_{k,\sigma}\epsilon_k c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}c_{k\sigma} 
+ \sum_{\sigma}\epsilon_d d^{\dagger}_{\sigma}d_{\sigma} 
+ Ud^{\dagger}_{\uparrow}d_{\uparrow}d^{\dagger}_{\downarrow}d_{\downarrow}
+ \sum_{k,\sigma}V_k(d^{\dagger}_{\sigma}c_{k\sigma} + c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}d_{\sigma})</math>,

where the <math>c</math> operator is the [[Creation and annihilation operators|annihilation operator]] of a conduction electron, and <math>d</math> is the annihilation operator for the impurity, <math>k</math> is the conduction electron [[wavevector]], <math>\sigma</math> labels the [[Spin (physics)|spin]]. The unperturbed single-electron energy, relative to the [[Fermi level]], is <math>\epsilon_k</math> for the conduction electrons and <math>\epsilon_d</math> for impurity electrons. The The on–site Coulomb repulsion is <math>U</math>, and <math>V</math> gives the hybridization.

== Regimes ==
The model yields several regimes that depend on the relationship of the impurity energy levels to the [[Fermi level]] <math>E_{\rm F}</math>:<ref name="Rhyno 2017">{{cite web |last1=Rhyno |first1=Brendan |title=Two-Impurity Kondo Physics |url=https://guava.physics.ucsd.edu/~nigel/Courses/Web%20page%20563/Essays_2017/PDF/Rhyno_version_2.pdf |website=Physics 563: Phase Transitions and the Renormalization Group |publisher=UCSD |access-date=9 September 2026}}</ref>
*The ''empty orbital'' regime for <math>\epsilon_d \gg E_{\rm F}</math>, and the ''full orbital'' regime for <math>\epsilon_d+U \ll E_{\rm F}</math>, which have no local moment.
*The ''intermediate'' regime for <math>\epsilon_d\approx E_{\rm F}</math> or <math>\epsilon_d+U\approx E_{\rm F}</math>.
*The ''local moment'' regime for <math>\epsilon_d \ll E_{\rm F} \ll \epsilon_d+U</math>, which yields a magnetic moment at the impurity.

In the local moment regime, the magnetic moment is present at the impurity site. However, for low enough temperature, the moment is [[Kondo effect|Kondo]] screened to give non-magnetic many-body singlet state.<ref name="Schrieffer-Wolff" /><ref name="Hewson1993" />

== Heavy-fermion systems ==
For heavy-fermion systems, a lattice of impurities is described by the periodic Anderson model.<ref name="Hewson1993" /> The one-dimensional model is

:<math>H = \sum_{k,\sigma}\epsilon_k c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}c_{k\sigma} 
+ \sum_{j,\sigma}\epsilon_f f^{\dagger}_{j\sigma}f_{j\sigma} 
+ U\sum_{j}f^{\dagger}_{j\uparrow}f_{j\uparrow}f^{\dagger}_{j\downarrow}f_{j\downarrow}
+ \sum_{j,k,\sigma}V_{jk}(e^{ikx_j}f^{\dagger}_{j\sigma}c_{k\sigma} + e^{-ikx_j}c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}f_{j\sigma})</math>,

where <math>x_j</math> is the position of impurity site <math>j</math>, and <math>f</math> is the impurity creation operator (used instead of <math>d</math> by convention for heavy-fermion systems). The hybridization term allows ''f''-[[atomic orbital|orbital]] electrons in heavy fermion systems to interact, although they are separated by a distance greater than the [[Hill limit (solid-state)|Hill limit]].

== Other variants ==
There are other variants of the Anderson model, such as the [[Special unitary group|SU(4)]] Anderson model{{citation needed|date=April 2021}}, which is used to describe impurities which have an orbital, as well as a spin, degree of freedom. This is relevant in [[carbon nanotube quantum dot]] systems. The SU(4) Anderson model Hamiltonian is

:<math>H = \sum_{k,\sigma}\epsilon_k c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}c_{k\sigma} 
+ \sum_{i,\sigma}\epsilon_d d^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}d_{i\sigma} 
+ \sum_{i,\sigma,i'\sigma '} \frac{U}{2}n_{i\sigma}n_{i'\sigma '}
+ \sum_{i,k,\sigma}V_k(d^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{k\sigma} + c^{\dagger}_{k\sigma}d_{i\sigma})</math>,

where <math>i</math> and ''<math>i'</math>'' label the orbital degree of freedom (which can take one of two values), and ''<math>n</math>'' represents the [[number operator]] for the impurity.
